note: Original Panta Rhei prompt deck, written for this project. Inspired by the idea of Brian Eno and Peter Schmidt's Oblique Strategies (1975); none of their card texts are used or adapted. Drawn by create.oblique-prompts. CC BY 4.0.
prompts: Make the smallest version that could still surprise someone.
Explain it to a seven-year-old. Keep only what survives.
Price it at zero. Who pays now?
Price it at a thousand times more. What must it become?
Move it to a different century.
Give it to the person least likely to want it.
Do the slow part first.
Make the invisible part visible.
Make the visible part disappear.
Hand the hardest step to the customer, on purpose.
What would this look like as a ritual?
Turn the waiting time into the product.
Borrow the rules of a game you played as a child.
Make it work at night, in silence.
Split it into two things that need each other.
Merge it with the thing it competes with.
Solve it completely for one named person.
Solve it for a million people, badly.
What would the person who cleans the building suggest?
Write the complaint letter first.
Make it portable. Then make it immovable.
Let it fail in public, gracefully.
Change who it is for, not what it is.
Keep the form; change the material.
Keep the material; change the form.
Add a deadline that cannot move.
Remove the deadline entirely.
Make it something people do together.
Make it something people do alone.
Find what everyone throws away and use it.
Put it in the place it least belongs.
What would it sound like?
Charge for the part you give away; give away the part you charge for.
Design the ending first.
Copy nature's laziest solution.
What if volunteers had to build it?
Make it last a hundred years.
Make it last one hour.
Name it before you build it.
What would a rule-breaker in your field do on their first day?
